correctness.rationale: For any triple in the ternary quandle-operation relation, all 30 atomic equality/operation facts are equivalent to nine explicit linear congruence indicators. Three-round back-and-forth is exactly the set of all two-pebble extension profiles after the first move; translations make first pebbles interchangeable. For every modulus at least nine, the only witness-dependent congruence solutions lie among at most eight exceptional residues; a generic witness necessarily exists. The overlaps among exceptional residues depend exclusively on parity, additive order truncated at five, and solvability of doubling. The eleven possible profile sets are listed explicitly in RESULT.md. For moduli at least nine their occurrence pattern is determined exactly by divisibility by 2,3,4,8. The six smaller exceptions, the stable order-seven representative, and all fourteen pairwise distinct class signatures are established by literal enumeration of 30 atomic facts in verify.py and the exact type_certificate.json. The sharp bound 24 follows because the stable gcd-24 class has no index below 24. The regression checks for moduli 9 through 500 corroborate, but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary literature proves isomorphism and automorphism classifications of finite quandles, not three-round equivalence in the pure ternary operation-graph language. The result supplies an exact fourteen-class quotient of an infinite family, including an arithmetic gcd-24 law and six exceptional singleton theories. Targeted semantic searches for dihedral/Takasaki kei, first-order rank three, Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé equivalence, and broader Alexander-quandle coverage did not identify a prior implication of the claimed theorem. This is a best-knowledge finding, not an assertion that all historical literature has been exhaustively checked.

value.rationale: The object is the standard finite dihedral/Takasaki quandle, a canonical reflection/Alexander quandle family used in knot invariants and finite algebra. The invariant is not an arbitrary statistic: it is the complete three-round first-order theory in the natural relational presentation of the operation. The result gives an unexpected arithmetic stabilization by \(\gcd(n,24)\), precisely six exceptional small indices, fourteen nontrivial logical theories, and a sharp bound of twenty-four on the least representative. Unlike a small known-table recomputation, the theorem covers every modulus by a structural congruence reduction and explains exactly which moduli shallow logic can and cannot distinguish.
